test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 19 Jan 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT a style of Hindustani classical music?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Alapana.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hindustani classical music** is the classical music of the Indian subcontinent's** northern regions.**
 
• It's also known as **Shastriya sangeet** or **North Indian classical music.**
 
• Its roots can be traced back to the **12th century CE** when it split from Carnatic music, the southern classical tradition.
 
• **Dhrupad, Khyal, and Tarana** are the** three major vocal genres** or styles associated with Hindustani classical music.
 
• Dhamar, Trivat, Chaiti, Kajari, Tappa, Tap-Khyal, Ashtapadis, Thumri, Dadra, Ghazal, and Bhajan are** light classical genres **that do not follow the strict principles of classical music.
 
• **Tansen** is widely regarded as the **founder of Hindustani music.**
 
• Alapana__:
 __
 
• The exposition of a raga or tone is known as alapana or ragam.
 
• It is the first element of Ragam Tanam Pallavi (RTP), which demonstrates a Carnatic musician's ability to comprehend a raga and compose music to accompany it.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Thumri__:**

 __
 
• ​Thumri is the most famous** light-classical music** form in **North India,** founded at the court of **Lucknow's king Wajid Ali Shah **in the **19th century.**
 
• It has strong ties to** kathak,** the principal classical dance form of North India, of which the Shah was a leading exponent.
 
• The word** "thumri"** comes from the Hindi verb **thumuknaa**, which means "to walk with a dancing gait in such a way that the ankle-bells tinkle."
 
 
 
• **Dhrupad__:**
 __
 
• It is the** oldest known style **of major vocal style associated with Hindustani classical music, **Haveli Sangeet of Pushtimarg Sampraday,** and is also related to the **South Indian Carnatic **tradition.
 
• Apart from the Dagar tradition, the **Darbhanga tradition** is one of the two primary living Dhrupad Gharanas.
 
• Dhrupad's Darbhanga gharana is represented by the** Mallik family.**
 
• The **founders** of the tradition are** Radha Krishna and Karta Ram,** the court musicians for the **Nawab of Darbhanga.**
 
• The **primary instrument** used for dhrupad has been the **Rudra Veena**, but the surbahar and the Sursringar are also used.
 
 
 
• **Tappa__:**​
 
 
• Tappa is a type of** semi-classical **Indian vocal music.
 
• Its specialty is a **rapid, nuanced, and knotty** composition with a rolling rhythm.
 
• Its melodies are beautiful and pleasant, and they portray a** lover's emotional outbursts.**
 
• Tappe were usually sung in **royal courts** by songstresses known as** Baigees.**
 
• **Shori Mian**, also known as **Mian Ghulam Nabi Shori,** was an Indian Hindustani classical music composer who lived from **1742 to 1792.**
 
• **Asaf-Ud-Dowlah, Nawab of Awadh,** employed him as a court singer. **In Punjab,** he composed tappa, one of the most difficult classical genres.
